incidents.name: Pricer ownership manager unrestricted transferOwnership
incidents.notes: The pricer-ownership manager deployed with the December oracle upgrade exposed transferOwnership(address,address) with no caller restriction, so the attacker took ownership of the stETH/AAVE/LINK/WBTC pricer proxies, swapped in a malicious pricer implementation, wrote arbitrary expiry prices into the Opyn Oracle and redeemed worthless oTokens against the MarginPool.

sources.ref: callTracer review of the takeover tx: attacker helper 0x1a7efc51... calls 0x9d7b3586... with selector 0x6d435421 (transferOwnership(address,address)), which forwards f2fde38b to pricer proxy 0xa4aC089B972206021EceB50a494d60B1c74E534e, then setImplementation (0xd784d426) to malicious pricer 0xE1f09d50F733993b11bF3054bD870d688401984c and pushes an expiry price into Oracle 0xb5711dAeC960c9487d95bA327c570a7cCE4982c0; the same pattern repeats for 0xb78E96750497e319Bb6a09a8Dc7C75fE32937AdA. Victim creator 0xb594f7e7ad548f63db49665ae4e3d3f8457cf6f5 is not the attacker; the MarginPool drain followed 10 blocks later in tx 0x16eded2553e0793472a6283093738152de1dd0e2504836856fbcaf88cc4a2687 Recheck of the deployment basis (DELEGATECALL audit): the victim's fallback is a non-standard proxy path that DELEGATECALLs whatever address sits in plain storage slot 1 (no EIP-1967 or beacon slot is used); slot 1 reads 0x0 at the incident block 23995254, so that path dead-ends in STOP and every executed instruction comes from the victim's own runtime, which is byte-identical at the creation block 23979057 and the incident block 23995254. The only other DELEGATECALL is an OpenZeppelin Address helper on a target passed in by the caller. Deployment is therefore the right basis, and the flawed transferOwnership(address,address) is code the deployer shipped 2.3 days earlier, not something the attacker installed.
